events.text: The cloud trial of your order is held on a platform that drifts out over the open sky, so that a junior who loses steps off it in front of everyone. The register's ninth place is called first. Your name is on the list.

choices.text: Fight your way up the register

ok.log: You step off the platform at the end of the day standing on your own feet, and the register has your name higher on it.

fail.log: You step off it the other way. The register does not change for you this time.

choices.text: Yield your bout to a junior who needs it more

effects.log: You bow out of your bout. The junior wins it, and an ancestor in the back row notices.

events.text: Every five years the juniors of the order are ranked again, and every five years someone weeps on the steps. This year the elders have set the trial as a single long climb up a stair of cloud that thins as you go.

choices.text: Climb until the stair runs out

ok.log: You climb past the place the stair should have run out, and the elders write your name a little higher.

fail.log: The stair runs out under you before the others'. You climb back down to where your name stays.

choices.text: Walk beside a junior who is struggling, and finish last together

effects.log: You finish last, together. An ancestor in the high window watches you do it.

events.text: The trial is a single bout this year, against whoever the elders draw from the jade jar. They draw a name and read it out, and the junior who stands up is one you have trained beside for decades.

choices.text: Fight them properly, as a friend should

ok.log: It is a good bout. You win it, and you help them up, and the register has your name higher.

fail.log: It is a good bout. They win it, and help you up, and the register stays as it was for you.

choices.text: Let them have it

effects.log: You lose on purpose and do it well enough that only the ancestors can tell.

events.text: The elders have put your name forward: the order needs an heir, and the long hall will count its stones in two years. Each faction sends someone to your grotto the same evening, not knowing about the other.

choices.text: Speak for yourself in the long hall

effects.log: You speak, and the first faction listens harder than the second.

choices.text: Work the side halls quietly

effects.log: You work the side halls. The second faction finds you easier to like than they expected.

choices.text: Stay out of it and let them decide

effects.log: You stay out of it. The ancestors approve; the factions are not sure what to make of you.

events.text: An Isle Ancestor you have only ever seen at a distance stops you on the stair. "They will vote on you as heir," the ancestor says. "I have no vote. I only wanted to see your face when you heard."

choices.text: Speak for yourself in the long hall

effects.log: You speak, and the first faction listens harder than the second.

choices.text: Work the side halls quietly

effects.log: You work the side halls. The second faction finds you easier to like than they expected.

choices.text: Stay out of it and let them decide

effects.log: You stay out of it. The ancestors approve; the factions are not sure what to make of you.

events.text: The head of your order has failed the order for too long, and the elders say so out loud now. A vote is called to put the head out of the seat, and everyone in the long hall is looking at the seats nearest the top. Yours is one of them.

choices.text: Speak for yourself in the long hall

effects.log: You speak, and the first faction listens harder than the second.

choices.text: Work the side halls quietly

effects.log: You work the side halls. The second faction finds you easier to like than they expected.

choices.text: Stay out of it and let them decide

effects.log: You stay out of it. The ancestors approve; the factions are not sure what to make of you.

events.text: The order's head has not come out of the grotto in nine years, and the orders around it have begun to take isles that were never offered. The elders call the vote. Someone has to be ready to sit down when the seat is empty.

choices.text: Speak for yourself in the long hall

effects.log: You speak, and the first faction listens harder than the second.

choices.text: Work the side halls quietly

effects.log: You work the side halls. The second faction finds you easier to like than they expected.

choices.text: Stay out of it and let them decide

effects.log: You stay out of it. The ancestors approve; the factions are not sure what to make of you.

events.text: Thirty years in the First seat, and the ancestors have given their nod: the order will vote whether to make you Grand Elder, a seat that has stood empty since before the last gathering of the heavens.

choices.text: Speak for yourself in the long hall

effects.log: You speak, and the first faction listens harder than the second.

choices.text: Work the side halls quietly

effects.log: You work the side halls. The second faction finds you easier to like than they expected.

choices.text: Stay out of it and let them decide

effects.log: You stay out of it. The ancestors approve; the factions are not sure what to make of you.

events.text: The jade token of your order is a small thing, the size of a palm, and without it every order you give must be asked twice. {npc} has it, and has been seen wearing it openly on the Drifting Market, smiling.

choices.text: Go to the market and take it back

ok.log: You take it back in front of the whole market. {npc} keeps the scar and none of the token.

fail.log: {npc} keeps it, and keeps smiling, and the market keeps watching.

choices.text: Have a new token cut and let the old one go

effects.log: The new token is cut by the next gathering. Everyone knows it is not the old one.

events.text: A slip of jade comes to your grotto in the night, in {npc}'s hand: the token of your order will be at the old shrine on the Fifth Cloud at moonrise, and so will {he}, and so should you be, alone.

choices.text: Go alone

ok.log: You come back at moonset with the token on its cord and {npc} far behind you.

fail.log: You come back at moonset without it, and with a lesson about going alone.

choices.text: Do not go: cut a new one

effects.log: You stay home and have a new token cut. The order notices which kind of head you are.

events.text: Lanterns on the clouds at night, a whole line of them, coming up under the edge of your immortal house's isle where the wards are thinnest. Your disciples are already at the rail, looking back at you.

choices.text: Lead them to the edge

ok.log: The raiders go down off the isle faster than they climbed it, and your disciples talk about the night for years.

fail.log: They break through the thin wards and take what they came for before dawn.

choices.text: Pay them to turn back

effects.log: A chest goes over the rail on a rope. The lanterns turn back.

choices.text: Pull everyone back to the inner hall and let the stores go

effects.log: You keep every disciple and lose every store. The isle remembers both.

events.text: A rival from another isle has decided your immortal house is rich enough to be worth the trouble, and has come with three wing-captains to say so at your gate, quite politely.

choices.text: Answer them at the gate

ok.log: They leave less politely than they came, and one of the wing-captains is carried.

fail.log: They come through the gate politely and leave with your stores, just as politely.

choices.text: Offer a sum to see them gone

effects.log: They take it, bow, and go. Next time they will bring four captains.

events.text: An elder of an order you owe a favour to arrives on your isle with a jade slip and a very patient face. The favour is being called in: a season of your sword on a far isle, for a quarrel that is not yours.

choices.text: Go, and pay the debt in person

effects.log: You go. The quarrel is not yours, and you settle it anyway.

choices.text: Send stones instead of yourself

effects.log: The elder accepts the stones with a face that says they will remember it.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: The elder writes your refusal on the slip, very neatly, and leaves.

events.text: "You remember the favour," says the slip from the order you owe. "We need it now: stand beside us at the Jade Court when the old quarrel is heard, and say what you saw."

choices.text: Stand beside them at the Court

effects.log: You stand beside them and say what you saw. The debt is paid, and some others now owe you a look.

choices.text: Send a gift and a letter of regret

effects.log: They take the gift. They read the letter twice.

choices.text: Send nothing

effects.log: The slip is not answered. That is an answer too.

events.text: Every five years your order and a rival order meet on a platform between their isles, three juniors from each, one after another, the winner staying on. This year the elders have written your name among the three.

choices.text: Step onto the platform with the other two

effects.log: You step up with them. The rival order's three are already waiting.

choices.text: Give your place to a younger junior

effects.log: You give your place away. The younger one goes white, then very determined.

events.text: The exchange match between the orders is a custom older than anyone in either of them. Your elder hands you the order's sash for the day and says only: "Try to come back across the platform on your own feet."

choices.text: Wear the sash

effects.log: You tie the sash on. The platform is very small and the drop on either side is very large.

choices.text: Hand the sash to someone else

effects.log: The elder takes the sash back without comment, which is its own comment.

events.text: On the white step of the Jade Court, before witnesses of the five orders, you hold up your jade pendant, the one you have worn since you first came above the clouds, and the whole court waits for the sound it makes when it breaks.

choices.text: Break it

effects.log: It breaks cleanly, in two. The court lets out its breath together.

choices.text: Break it, and say a word for those you fought

effects.log: You break it, and say the names of three who fell to you. Some of the witnesses look away.

events.text: The witnesses have come from every isle that ever quarrelled with you, which is a great many. They watch you break the pendant with an interest that is not quite trust. Up here, a promise is a long thing.

choices.text: Bow to each of them

effects.log: You bow to every one, which takes until evening. By the last bow some of them believe you.

choices.text: Walk away without looking back

effects.log: You walk away. They will watch you for a thousand years, and you know it.

events.text: Your new kin of the Isles are a house that has married into other houses for ten thousand years, and they have come with their marriage terms written on jade, as they always do. The elders of the house wait to hear which you will take.

choices.text: A dowry: a scroll of their house's method

effects.log: The scroll comes with the bride-price. It is very old and very good.

choices.text: A child of the marriage, promised to them

effects.log: The terms are written: a child, when grown, goes to their house.

choices.text: A war pledge: their champion in your wars, you in theirs

effects.log: The terms are written in two copies, and each house keeps one.

choices.text: No terms: only the marriage

effects.log: The house is surprised, and then rather pleased.

events.text: The Red Thread Elder of the Jade Court has written the marriage, and now the house you married into asks for terms, as old houses do: something given, something promised, or something sworn.

choices.text: A dowry: a scroll of their house's method

effects.log: The scroll comes with the bride-price. It is very old and very good.

choices.text: A child of the marriage, promised to them

effects.log: The terms are written: a child, when grown, goes to their house.

choices.text: A war pledge: their champion in your wars, you in theirs

effects.log: The terms are written in two copies, and each house keeps one.

choices.text: No terms: only the marriage

effects.log: The house is surprised, and then rather pleased.
